chapter: Own bands and Los Angeles clubs
title: The record band and Kay Starr's hits recorded at Capitol
summary: Lee describes recording in the Capitol president's office, where two Kay Starr hits were made, and earning two or three hundred dollars a session.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Uh huh. Capital was at Sunset and Vine.
We used to go up the back.
That was kind of cute. Well, I might as well tell that.

Because it could be told later on, okay. Well, during that record band, that's where 2 of Kay Starr's hits were made, during the record band, and Capital was right next to Wallachs, and they had the offices upstairs, and they set up a recording thing in the President's office. They set up the whole recording thing, and we used to go up there, and we did 2 things that Kay Starr had smashes of.
Oh, I told you about me and titles, but
maybe I can find out about them later on and let you know. But she had 2 hits right up there in that room.
The President was Clyde Wallach then? Johnny Mercer?

No. It was the one that married one of the King Sisters. What was his name? He married one of the King Sisters. I can see him; I can always see the people, but I forget their names. Nice man. Now I draw a blank on him, but I'll think of his name.
Well anyway, that was what we were doing then, and you made more money doing the record band than you made when it was legit. Yeah, because they pay you two and three hundred dollars, you know.

They played two or three hundred dollars a session, you know, and so you get a couple of sessions a week, and we were all right. And all the big names that we know out here, they were doing it, too. But this is going to be for posterity so it can't hurt anyone. Nobody will hurt.
